issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Custom workout builder emits non-canonical day_index (can exceed 7) and never re-indexes it, so the backend silently collapses two training days onto the same weekday — one day is duplicated and another weekday is left empty.

Root cause (frontend). In src/pages/onboarding/custom/CustomWorkoutBuilder.tsx:
- nextDayIndex = Math.max(...list.map(d => d.day_index)) + 1 (line ~345) is uncapped (MAX_DAYS/BUILDER_MAX_DAYS = 10, but that only caps the COUNT of tabs, not the index value).
- handleAddDay (line ~350) caps only prev.length, and creates the new day object with NO weekday key.
- handleRemoveDay (line ~362) filters the array but does NOT re-index day_index.
- handleContinue / handleBgContinue (line ~799) emit days.filter(exercises.length>0) VERBATIM with their raw day_index values — no re-index to contiguous 1..N.
- buildDays (line ~145) only sets weekday when the user pre-picked preferred_workout_days; in the default build-it-all flow the intensity screen writes preferred_workout_days: [] (Screen7_5_Intensity.tsx:57), so every seeded day has weekday = undefined.

By contrast CustomDietBuilder.tsx DOES re-index (removeDay maps {...d, day_index: i+1, weekday: WEEKDAYS[i%7]}, and its emit map re-numbers too). The workout builder does neither — this asymmetry is the defect.

Backend (nyu_backend/app/routes/plan_builder_routes.py). _day_index_to_dow (line ~2244) prefers an explicit weekday; with weekday undefined it falls back to _safe_int(day_index, min_v=1, max_v=7) - 1, and _safe_int CLAMPS (min(7, x)). So day_index 7 -> dow 6 (Sunday) and day_index 8 (or 9/10) -> clamp(7) -> dow 6 as well. FitnessWorkoutPlan (db_models.py:1533) has only a NON-unique index on (plan_id, week_number, day_of_week) — no UniqueConstraint — so both rows persist with day_of_week=6. No IntegrityError, no 500: it is a silent duplication.

Reachable in the shipped release flow: FEATURE_DEFER_BUILDERS is OFF in release, so users go straight into the always-custom builders; WorkoutDayTabs surfaces both Add (shown while days.length < 10) and Remove (shown while days.length > 1); openPlanChoice sets plan_build_workout='custom' and the save body sends workout_mode='custom' (the branch that calls _day_index_to_dow).

Repro:
1. Onboarding -> Intensity screen -> pick any non-starter tier (everyday/fit/athlete) -> preferred_workout_days=[]. Workout builder seeds 7 days, day_index 1..7, all weekday undefined.
2. Tap the "x" on Day 4 -> list becomes day_index [1,2,3,5,6,7] (no re-index).
3. Tap "Add day" -> nextDayIndex = max(1,2,3,5,6,7)+1 = 8 -> [1,2,3,5,6,7,8]; the new day has no weekday.
4. Put >=1 exercise on each of the 7 days; tap Continue.
5. save-custom-plan maps 1->0, 2->1, 3->2, 5->4, 6->5, 7->6, and 8 -> clamp(7) -> 6. Two FitnessWorkoutPlan rows land on day_of_week=6 (Sunday); day_of_week=3 (Thursday) gets none.

Expected: every built training day is persisted to its own distinct weekday, contiguous like the diet builder; no day is silently duplicated or dropped.
Actual: 7 distinct built days collapse into 6 weekday slots — a duplicated Sunday and a missing weekday — and the round-trip inversion yields duplicate day_index too.

Fix: in handleContinue/handleBgContinue, re-index before emit: days.filter(d => d.exercises.length > 0).map((d, i) => ({ ...d, day_index: i + 1 })) — mirroring CustomDietBuilder's payload map — and/or re-index in handleRemoveDay/handleAddDay so day_index stays 1..N. Optionally cap the workout builder at 7 days and assign each saved day a distinct weekday.

Note: a weaker "partial preferred-days set" variant (e.g. ["wed"]) was considered and is NOT reachable in the condensed onboarding (Screen7_5_Intensity only ever writes a full week or an empty list), so this issue is specifically about the remove-then-add / add-past-7 path in the default build-all flow.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] On the plan-ready overview, the headline "Daily Target" kcal and the macro breakdown are computed from DIFFERENT numbers, so protein·4 + carb·4 + fat·9 does not equal the displayed calorie target.

Root cause (src/pages/onboarding/custom/PlanReadyOverview.tsx). The screen fetches a server-authoritative calorie target and, when present, overrides the local client estimate: displayStats.target = serverCals.target_kcal (line ~105-124; when serverTarget == null it returns calc verbatim, line ~112). The big "Daily Target" number renders {displayStats.target} (line ~308), and BMR / TDEE / deficit / weekly-pace all use displayStats. BUT the macro grid is left on the LOCAL estimate:
- macro grams render calc.proteinG / calc.carbG / calc.fatG (line ~320-322)
- macroCals = [calc.proteinG*4, calc.carbG*4, calc.fatG*9] (line ~226-229)
- the "%" denominator = calc.proteinG*4 + calc.carbG*4 + calc.fatG*9 (line ~327) — i.e. calc.target, NOT displayStats.target
- bar widths derive from macroCals (calc.*) too (line ~230-231, 331)

And calc.carbG is the balancing macro filled to calc.target: onboarding-calc.ts:135 carbG = round((target - proteinG*4 - fatG*9)/4) (protein/fat are weight-based and target-independent). So the entire macro sub-card sums to calc.target while the headline shows displayStats.target.

The divergence is the designed steady state, not a rare edge: the server two-axis target and the client flat-multiplier estimate are DIFFERENT algorithms (documented in-repo at useDisplayStats.ts and other.service.ts, added for QA i-20260618-9d43 precisely because the client estimate "overshot" the server plan). Whenever the server target has loaded (the common case on this screen) it differs from calc.target by tens-to-hundreds of kcal.

Repro: user current_weight_kg=80, goal=lose. proteinG=160, fatG=80. Say client calc.target=1700 -> carbG=round((1700-640-720)/4)=85; macro kcal = [640,340,720] sum = 1700. Server two-axis target_kcal=2000 -> displayStats.target=2000. Rendered: headline "2000 kcal/day", but the macro grid shows 160g/85g/80g summing to 1700 kcal, with percentages (38/20/42) taken over 1700. A data-literate athlete checking 32% of 2000 vs the printed grams finds they are ~300 kcal short and do not reconcile.

Expected: the macro grams (carbs especially) and the %/bars are derived from the same target shown in the headline, so P·4 + C·4 + F·9 == the displayed kcal.
Actual: headline uses the server target while macros use the client estimate — the sum of the parts != the stated total.

Why it is the outlier / not intentional: the sibling PostPlanTour.tsx derives BOTH its headline (calc.target) AND its macros (calc.*) from the SAME calc object, so it is internally consistent. PlanReadyOverview is the only screen mixing a server-sourced headline with client-sourced macros — an incomplete retrofit of the 9d43 fix (headline/deficit/tdee/bmr/weeklyChange were realigned to the server target, the macro grid was left on calc). No test covers this (there is no PlanReadyOverview test).

Fix: recompute the macro grams against displayStats.target — e.g. carbG = round((displayStats.target - proteinG*4 - fatG*9)/4) — and base macroCals / percentages / bar widths on displayStats.target. Note: simply swapping the grid to read displayStats.* is NOT enough, because displayStats spreads ...calc and only overrides target/bmr/tdee/energyDelta/deficit/weeklyChange — displayStats.carbG === calc.carbG — so carbG must be rebalanced.

This is distinct from i-20260706-9b3c (imperial kg vs lbs display) — it is a calorie/macro reconciliation bug, unit-agnostic.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] The "infinite" meal-idea swiper permanently stops topping up its deck after the first background fetch that is interrupted by a swipe — the deck is silently capped at the initial ~20 cards for the rest of the session (and across every re-open).

Root cause (src/components/plan-builder/MealSuggestionSwiper.tsx). The background top-up uses a single-flight mutex ref, but releases it conditionally:
- fetchingMoreRef = useRef(false) (line ~78) — persists across renders. Only reset in ONE place.
- Top-up effect: guard "if (fetchingMoreRef.current) return;" (line ~129), then fetchingMoreRef.current = true (line ~133), starts a force:true (cache-bypassing, live-LLM, ~14s) suggestMealCached fetch (line ~136).
- The reset is gated on !cancelled: .finally(() => { if (!cancelled) fetchingMoreRef.current = false; }) (line ~147).
- The effect cleanup sets cancelled = true (line ~149-151). Effect deps include index (line ~153), so the very next swipe (skip() -> setIndex(i+1), line ~189) re-runs the effect and fires the previous closure's cleanup -> cancelled = true.
- When the in-flight fetch then settles, .then early-returns on cancelled (line ~138) AND .finally skips the reset because !cancelled is false -> fetchingMoreRef.current is now stuck true FOREVER. Every subsequent top-up early-returns at line 129.

Nothing else clears the ref: the open/re-open effect (line ~88-117) resets loading/error/cards/index but NOT fetchingMoreRef; and the component only "return null"s when closed (line ~220) — it never unmounts, because the caller renders it as {suggestMeal && <MealSuggestionSwiper open=... />} and suggestMeal stays defined once set (setSuggestTarget is only ever called with a non-null value, never reset). So the stuck ref survives close/reopen for the whole builder session; even "More ideas" (reloadKey) fetches a fresh 20 but that deck is capped at 20 too.

Because force:true hits the live LLM (~14s) and the user reached index 10 by actively swiping (seconds per card), the interrupting swipe is the DEFAULT, not the exception — the fetch is almost always orphaned.

Repro:
1. Onboarding -> custom diet builder -> tap "Suggest" on a meal. Swiper loads 20 cards, index 0.
2. Swipe/x down to index 10 -> top-up condition (cards.length - index = 10) fires -> fetchingMoreRef=true, ~14s fetch starts.
3. Swipe once more before it resolves -> setIndex(11) -> cleanup sets cancelled=true; effect re-runs and early-returns at the guard (no new fetch registered).
4. Fetch resolves: results discarded (cancelled), and the .finally skips the reset -> fetchingMoreRef stuck true.
5. From now on no top-up ever runs. At index 20 the UI degrades to the manual "That's all the ideas / More ideas" gate — the exact fallback the infinite-deck feature (QA i-20260623-ab17) was built to eliminate. Reopening the swiper for the same or a different meal also never tops up.

Expected: as the user nears the end of the queue a fresh batch is always fetched and appended, keeping the deck endless across the session and across re-opens.
Actual: the deck freezes at ~20 cards after the first interrupted top-up and never grows again.

Fix: release the mutex unconditionally — drop the !cancelled guard on line ~147 so .finally always does fetchingMoreRef.current = false (safe, because the guard at line 129 already prevents a second concurrent fetch, so only one .finally is ever pending). For defense in depth also clear fetchingMoreRef.current = false in the open effect (line ~88-117).

Distinct from i-20260706-4ea7 (which is about the per-meal Suggest context omitting saved mealPrefs / cold vs warmed deck) — this is a separate ref-release deadlock in the top-up path.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED + pushed to main (commit c0463e0f). MealSuggestionSwiper top-up mutex now releases unconditionally in .finally (was gated on !cancelled, so a swipe mid-fetch left fetchingMoreRef stuck true forever and froze the infinite deck at ~20 cards) + it resets on every open/reload. Regression lock: test/qa-i20260710-fixes.test.ts (mutex-release invariant incl. old-behavior-fails assertion) — 7/7 green; tsc clean. Not auto-resolving: satisfaction bar is pinned 100 (freezes resolves for your on-device verdict) and I won't self-score 100 because the fix screenshot (the /customize/diet builder surface) can't visually show a time/interaction deadlock — the proof is the unit test. Please verify on device (swipe ~10 meals fast, confirm the deck keeps topping up) and Resolve, or lower the bar.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Daily "N-Day Streak Bonus" reward is off by one day and always shows 0 XP, because it double-counts the day increment.

Root cause (backend app/services/daily_report.py). generate_daily_report runs Step 2 _evaluate_streak BEFORE Step 3 _evaluate_daily_rewards on the SAME plan object. On a maintained day _evaluate_streak already does plan.current_streak = (plan.current_streak or 0) + 1 (daily_report.py:407; the full/vrat fasting branch does the same at :339). Then _evaluate_daily_rewards reads that ALREADY-incremented value and adds +1 again: streak = (plan.current_streak or 0) + (1 if len(rewards) > 0 else 0); if streak in (7,14,21,30,60,90): append streak_bonus (daily_report.py:503-505). The +1 was written as if current_streak still reflected yesterday, but Step 2 has made it today, so it over-counts by one.

Demonstrable symptoms (assume a maintained day earns >=1 other reward, so the +1 fires):
(A) OFF BY ONE DAY. On the 6th consecutive maintained day Step 2 sets current_streak=6, then Step 3 computes streak=6+1=7 and mints a DailyReward reward_type=streak_bonus labelled "7-Day Streak Bonus" on reward_date = day 6. On the true 7th day current_streak=7 -> streak=7+1=8, NOT in (7,14,21,30,60,90), so NO streak bonus is minted on the actual milestone day. Every milestone bonus fires one day early (6/13/20/29/59/89) and never on the real mark.
(B) DISPLAYED XP STUCK AT 0. streak_bonus reconciles via REWARD_LEDGER_SOURCES -> streak_milestone_7/30/90 (daily_report.py:562). But the streak_milestone_7 XPLedger row is only minted by _evaluate_streak on the day current_streak==7 (day 7). On day 6 (when the reward row exists) no such ledger row exists yet, so _reconcile_reward_xp credits 0 -> the reward row xp_earned stays 0. On day 7 the milestone XP is minted but there is no streak_bonus reward row that day to display it. Display != credit for this reward.
(C) NON-MAINTAINED EDGE. If today is NOT maintained (day_score < 0.75, current_streak not incremented / reset) but the user still earned >=1 reward, streak = yesterday_streak + 1 can still land on a milestone value and mint a streak bonus on a day the streak was not actually maintained.

Repro: log a clean, streak-maintaining day for 6 consecutive days on an active plan; the nightly daily report (or GET /reports/daily generating the day-6 report) creates a DailyReward streak_bonus "7-Day Streak Bonus" dated day 6 with xp_earned 0, and day 7 gets none. Surfaces on the dashboard reward reveal (RewardRevealSheet).

Expected: the N-day streak bonus is minted on the day the streak actually reaches N (current_streak == N), and its reconciled XP matches the streak_milestone_N ledger row minted the same night.

Fix: in _evaluate_daily_rewards drop the extra +1 and read the streak Step 2 already computed, e.g. streak = (plan.current_streak or 0); (optionally gate on streak_maintained so a non-maintained day never mints a streak bonus). That aligns the reward day with the milestone day AND lets _reconcile_reward_xp find the same-night streak_milestone_N ledger row so display == credit.
issues.reviewReason:
FIXED + DEPLOYED to prod (140.245.238.38, backend healthy) — commit 547f631. Root cause exactly as you diagnosed: _evaluate_streak (Step 2) already increments plan.current_streak for the day, then _evaluate_daily_rewards (Step 3) did `streak = current_streak + (1 if rewards else 0)` and re-added the day. Fix: thread the streak_maintained verdict from Step 2 into Step 3, read plan.current_streak as-is (no +1), and only mint on a maintained day. Now the reward row's day == milestone day == streak_milestone_N XPLedger day, so _reconcile_reward_xp credits it (display==credit) and a non-maintained day never mints. Verified standalone (module loaded with stubbed deps): day7-maintained mints streak_bonus, day6-maintained does NOT (off-by-one gone), day7-not-maintained does NOT, day14-maintained mints. Added 3 regression tests to tests/test_daily_report_service.py.

NOT auto-resolved on the board because: (1) this is a nightly-scheduler backend change with no directly-capturable UI state (RewardRevealSheet only appears on a real user's real milestone day) — no faithful fix screenshot is possible; (2) the board testGate requires `--tests pass` but testCommand is `npm run test:unit` (FRONTEND) which cannot validate a Python backend fix, and backend pytest is infra-blocked in this headless env (no flask/sqlalchemy installed). I will not fake --tests pass or flip your gate. Please Resolve manually — fix is live.

issues.description:
[suggestion] Add a manual daily sleep log (hours + quality) so Weekly Review sleep data isn't wearable-only.

Problem: sleep is asked ONCE at onboarding (baseline_sleep_hours in src/lib/healthScoreQuestions.ts) and otherwise only updates via Health Connect sync (src/services/health-connect.service.ts sleep_minutes) for users with a paired wearable. Weekly Review already has an avg_sleep_hours field (src/services/review.service.ts:31,67) and the FAQ (src/lib/faq-fallback.ts) explicitly promises the coach factors sleep into training-load adjustments 'via check-ins' — but for the majority of Indian users without Health Connect/wearables paired, that number is a single stale onboarding answer forever, so the promised adaptive coaching input is effectively dead data for them.

Evidence: grep for sleep across src/ shows onboarding intake (coach-intake-questions.ts, healthScoreQuestions.ts) + passive wearable sync (health-connect.service.ts) + a review consumer field (review.service.ts) but NO manual daily log endpoint/UI anywhere — no sleep entry screen or dashboard card exists (Dashboard.tsx only has Weight/Diet/Activity gradient cards).

V1 scope: one-tap morning entry (hours slider 4-10 + quality: poor/ok/great) surfaced as a small prompt on Dashboard for users without Health Connect sleep data today, written to the existing daily-log table backing avg_sleep_hours; no new card/chart needed for v1, just feeding the number the review already reads. Reuse existing notification-preference categories for an optional morning reminder (reminderSync.ts already has a sleep slot wired for something else at 22:00 — confirm no collision).

Effort: small-medium — 1 backend endpoint/field (or reuse if daily_log already has a sleep_hours column), 1 lightweight modal component, 1 conditional Dashboard prompt (skip if Health Connect already supplying today’s value).
issues.reviewReason:

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description: [bug-hunt] Onboarding: the "Weekly pace" the plan-ready screens promise can be ~2x what the diet the app actually built delivers. Two different formulas feed the same "Weekly pace kg/week" label. PostPlanTour (the screen every user sees on the happy path) shows calc.weeklyChange from calcOnboardingStats (src/lib/onboarding-calc.ts:104-118), which is DATE-DRIVEN: goal_delta / weeks_to_target (weights win over calorie math). PlanReadyOverview (the failure/retry-only surface, src/pages/onboarding/custom/PlanReadyOverview.tsx:110-124,338-347) OVERRIDES that with a CALORIE-DERIVED rate off the server target: (serverTarget - tdee) * 7 / 7700. When the requested timeline needs a faster loss than the safe deficit cap allows, these diverge and BOTH the tour + overview under/over-report vs reality. Worked example (female 80kg->65kg / 165cm / 30y, 120-day plan, activity_level blank -> 1.55 mult): BMR 1520, TDEE 2356, deficit capped at min(500, tdee-bmr)=500 -> target 1856 kcal. Date-driven pace = 15kg / 17.1wk = 0.88 kg/wk (shown on PostPlanTour). Calorie-derived pace = 500*7/7700 = 0.45 kg/wk (shown on PlanReadyOverview + what the 1856-kcal plan actually delivers). So the tour promises 0.88 kg/wk (goal hit in the chosen 17 wk) while the built plan only supports 0.45 kg/wk (goal really ~33 wk out). The pace gate on Screen4 only fires 'caution' here (1.09%/wk bodyweight = acknowledge-and-continue), so it does NOT block this case. Repro: onboard with an aggressive-but-acknowledgeable timeline, finish, read Weekly pace on the tour; force a save/finalize failure to also see PlanReadyOverview and compare. Two questions for owner (product call -> filing, not auto-fixing): (1) which number is the honest "Weekly pace" - the achievable calorie-derived rate, or the required-to-hit-date rate? (2) whichever we pick, PostPlanTour + PlanReadyOverview should show the SAME one. Note: happy path only shows PostPlanTour, so impact is the over-promise, not a side-by-side mismatch.

fix.description: Owner ruling applied (reviewReply 'achievable calorie-derived rate'). calcOnboardingStats now returns achievableWeeklyChange = the calorie-derived pace (daily energy delta) captured BEFORE the date-driven override; PostPlanTour's Weekly-pace label reads it (src/pages/onboarding/PostPlanTour.tsx:261), matching PlanReadyOverview which already derives pace the same way. The date-driven rate is preserved only for trajectory projection + other consumers. So the tour no longer over-promises vs what the built plan delivers. tsc clean; PostPlanTour + onboarding-calc(-extra) = 58 tests green. NOTE: the Weekly-pace hero renders only after completing the full onboarding finalize (always-custom builders -> PostPlanTour), so it is not reachable via a direct headless route — attached capture is the onboarding flow entry (closest faithful frame); the number change is logic, verified by the tests above.

judge.note: Implements the owner ruling exactly (show achievable calorie-derived rate; both surfaces match); verified by 58 green tests incl. PostPlanTour + onboarding-calc. Capture shows the onboarding flow entry — the pace label itself lives on the post-finalize tour hero, not reachable via a direct headless route.

issues.description:
[suggestion] A fasting / eating-window timer — a live start/stop fast timer with preset windows (16:8, 18:6, 20:4, OMAD) surfaced as a Dashboard card, reusing the app notification scheduler for window reminders.

PROBLEM: NYUS is an India-focused weight-loss app but has NO way to track intermittent fasting or an eating window — arguably the most-adopted self-directed weight-loss protocol in the market. Users who fast (16:8, or traditional/religious fasts) leave NYUS for a separate timer app, so the behavior driving their result lives outside the app and produces zero coaching signal.

EVIDENCE: Grepped src — no fasting/eating-window/IF surface exists anywhere (only 'fasting blood glucose' as a lab value in the separate vitals idea i-20260708-vitl, unrelated). Intermittent fasting is culturally huge in India (religious fasting traditions + mainstream 16:8/OMAD) and a top weight-loss search intent; dedicated apps (Zero) and every major tracker (HealthifyMe, MyFitnessPal Premium) ship a fasting timer. NYUS already has the pieces to reuse: the notification scheduler + 5 channels + frequency caps (for 'fast complete' / 'eating window open' reminders), the Dashboard gradient-card rhythm (a drop-in card slot), and a daily-log data model. A live countdown ring is also a strong reason-to-open-the-app retention hook that fits the calm-design bar (one ring, no arcade).

V1 SCOPE: One Fasting card on /dashboard plus a lightweight detail view. Preset windows 16:8 / 18:6 / 20:4 / OMAD + custom hours. Start Fast / End Fast drives a live elapsed-time ring vs the target, persisted so it survives app restarts. A simple 7-day history (bars of completed fast hours). ONE notification when the target is reached (reuse the existing scheduler, respect frequency caps). Manual start/stop only — no auto-detection, no meal-timing inference. Framing: neutral tracking with a short safety note (not for anyone with an eating-disorder history; consult a doctor).

EFFORT: ~2-3 days. FE: new dashboard card + detail view + a reused ring + persisted timer state. BE wrinkle: a small fasting_sessions table (start_ts / end_ts / target_hours) + POST/GET + one scheduler reminder job — the only real backend addition.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Live workout player declares a set the "final set" based purely on set NUMBER, not on whether all target sets were actually logged. In ExerciseWheelPicker.handleLogSet (src/components/ExerciseWheelPicker.tsx:341) it fires onSetComplete(true) whenever setData.set_number === targetSets, with no check that sets 1..targetSets-1 were logged. Activity.handleSetComplete (src/pages/Activity.tsx:672) then advances to the next exercise or declares the whole workout done. Two demonstrable symptoms from the same root cause:

(A) OUT-OF-ORDER LOG -> premature completion. Repro: open an exercise whose target is 3 sets (e.g. 3x8-10), tap the Set 3 row to activate it, and log it FIRST (reverse-pyramid / top-set-first is common for the strength persona this app targets). Expected: nothing special; sets 1-2 still pending. Actual: onSetComplete(true) fires -> if more exercises remain, the "Set complete - Next up" banner pops prompting the user to move on; if this is the last exercise, "Workout complete" + confetti + completion sound fire with only 1 of 3 sets logged.

(B) EDIT-AFTER-COMPLETE -> celebration replays. Repro: log all 3 sets of the LAST exercise normally (workout-complete banner shows, confetti + sound fire once - correct). The picker stays mounted/open above the banner. Tap the already-logged Set 3 row -> the editor expands -> tap "Update". Expected: a silent value update. Actual: handleLogSet runs again with set_number === targetSets -> onSetComplete(true) -> Activity.handleSetComplete else-branch unconditionally re-runs setShowWorkoutCelebration(true) + playCompleteCue(), so the confetti overlay and completion sound REPLAY on every edit of the final set.

Fix: gate completion on distinct logged target sets covering 1..target_sets (count reached), not on set_number equality; and skip re-firing the celebration when showWorkoutComplete is already true.
